question: Why do skilled golfers often putt worse when told to pay close attention to their stroke?
answer: Because attention breaks up a skill that runs best unwatched. In Beilock and colleagues' experiments, experienced golfers and footballers did worse when asked to monitor their technique, and better when given a distracting second task; novices showed the opposite. A practised move runs as one piece, and inspecting the parts takes it apart.
move: Once a skill is learned, watch the target, not your own hands.
ask: In a moment that matters, am I overthinking something I already know how to do?
source: Beilock et al., J Exp Psychol Appl, 2002
reference: Beilock, Carr, MacMahon & Starkes, When paying attention becomes counterproductive, Journal of Experimental Psychology: Applied, 2002
